# Retail Analytics for CPG Brands: A Guide to Driving Growth


By[Jacqueline Nance](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/jacqueline-nance-sps) , *Senior Content Marketing Manager*


Last Updated November 23, 2026


7 min read


In this article, learn about:


-


The types of retail analytics CPG brands use to make smarter business decisions


-


The three key data sources that power CPG retail analytics


-


How big data and retail analytics help CPG brands improve performance and drive growth


---


Strong sales in one market don't always translate to success in another. A product that sells steadily in Chicago might sit untouched on shelves in Dallas. For consumer packaged goods (CPG) brands, understanding what's behind those differences will reveal opportunities that sales figures alone might miss.


Retail analytics bring sales, inventory, and shopper data together to give brands a clearer picture of product performance. With the right insights, teams can anticipate demand, make better inventory decisions, and identify where there's room to grow.


This guide examines how CPG brands use retail analytics, the data behind them, and how those insights support smarter decisions and long-term growth.


**Related Reading:**[Data analytics for CPG companies](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/data-analytics-for-cpg-companies)


## How Does Retail Analytics Help CPG Brands Grow?


Retail analytics helps CPG brands grow by showing which products, retailers, and promotions earn the most, so teams can put effort where it pays off. Growth depends on data that is current, connected, and used.[Big data in retail](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/big-data-in-retail) is now the base for spotting trends and deciding which SKUs stores will need.


In a crowded CPG market, business leaders keep returning to the same questions:


-


Which marketing channels drive the most customer growth?


-


How much buying power do the best customers have?


-


Which product lines should expand?


-


When should discounts run, and for whom?


CPG brands already collect plenty of data to answer them. The gap is usually in investment, management, and acting on what the data shows. Analytics also help brands anticipate shifts in demand, which matters when the economy is unpredictable. Brands that connect retail and supply chain data can protect revenue and keep their products visible to shoppers.


The next step is choosing the right kind of analysis.[Descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/retail-data-explained-descriptive-predictive-and-prescriptive) each answer a different question, and most brands use all three.


**Related Reading:**[Data Analytics for CPG Companies](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/data-analytics-for-cpg-companies)


## What Types of Retail Analytics Do CPG Brands Use?


Understanding what shoppers buy is just one part of the picture. CPG brands also need to know which products sell together, what customers are likely to purchase next, and how pricing and promotions influence demand. Three types of retail analytics help answer these questions.


### Market basket analysis


Market basket analysis shows which products shoppers buy together. It rests on a simple idea: a shopper who picks up one product is likely to pick up another. Brands use those pairings to build bundles, plan displays, and decide which products to pitch to a retailer as a set. It is one of the most common analyses in marketing and retail.


### Predictive analytics


Predictive analytics uses past buying behavior to estimate what shoppers will do next. Brands can test different approaches, see how the market is likely to respond, and adjust strategy before demand shifts. Predictive models also feed[demand planning](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/demand-planning) , which turns those estimates into production and shipping plans.


### Pricing and promotional analytics


Pricing and promotional analytics show how shoppers respond when prices change. Brands can find the price that earns the most margin across different customer groups, brands, and markets. Social media analysis adds another view of buying patterns and helps shape promotional messages. For the trade side of this work, see how[trade promotions and allowances](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-are-trade-promotions-and-allowances) work and how[AI is changing trade spend](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-future-of-trade-spend-ai-driven-strategies) .


**Related Reading:**[Why Demand Forecasting Accuracy Starts Before the Forecast Runs](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/why-demand-forecasting-accuracy-starts-before-the-forecast-runs)


## What types of data power CPG analytics?


Three types of data drive CPG analytics: operational, observational, and sales data. Each shows a different part of how a product moves from the shelf to the shopper.


-


**Operational data** shows the practical steps a brand can take to sell more, such as which sales and publicity activities are working.


-


**Observational data** shows where products sit in the store and how they perform there. It reflects the results of a brand's plan and points to openings in the market.


-


**Sales data** shows how many units shoppers buy, at a given time, in one geography or across all of them.


The real value comes from combining the three. Sales figures say what sold. Observational and operational data help explain why, so teams can repeat the decisions that led to the best results. Many brands add[syndicated data](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/syndicated-data-for-cpgs) for a market-wide view, and retailer sell-through data such as the[EDI 852 product activity report](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-852-product-activity-report-spsa) for a closer look at individual stores.


## What Are the Benefits of Big Data and Retail Analytics for CPG Brands?


The main benefits of retail analytics for CPG brands are a clearer supply chain, tighter inventory, better-aimed promotions, more personal marketing, and a faster response to change. Brands also use the same data to develop products and plan their portfolio.


### A clearer supply chain


Analytics simplifies complex supply chain activity. Information flows more easily, redundant steps drop out, and costs come down. Brands get practical insight from planning through sourcing, production, warehousing, shipping, and the store. That kind of[visibility for suppliers](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/visibility-for-suppliers-and-cpgs) and CPGs is also one of the qualities of a[competitive CPG supply chain](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/6-qualities-of-a-competitive-cpg-supply-chain) .


### Tighter inventory


Data supports precise planning, forecasting, and inventory optimization. Brands use storage space, cash, and labor more efficiently and carry less unsold stock. Combined data across regions and divisions lowers overflow costs and lets brands focus on their most profitable products. Metrics such as[gross margin return](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-gross-margin-return-on-inventory-investment-gmroi) on inventory investment show which products earn their shelf space.


### Better-aimed promotions


Product marketing depends on shopper choice. Data from social media, web pages, and user registrations helps brands:


-


Make each communication channel work harder


-


Judge whether a campaign is practical before launch


-


Track key performance indicators (KPIs)


-


Understand how shoppers buy


It also shows shopping habits, preferences, and sentiment, which improves both the strategy and how it is carried out. A complete analytics framework can raise return on investment (ROI) for marketing spend.[Best practices to drive sell-through](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/best-practices-to-drive-sell-through) show how to connect that spend to results at the shelf.


### More personal marketing


Brands have many insights into how shoppers spend. A single view of the shopper, linked to purchase patterns and sales, makes it easier to send messages that are timely and relevant. As data and analytics improve, marketers can build more personal experiences across every channel and stage of the shopping trip.


### A faster response to change


Analytics helps brands see shifts in who is buying and ride out sudden swings in the market. Teams make sharper decisions and act sooner on what the data shows. The same habit helps with outside shocks, as in this look at how[leading CPG brands use AI to get ahead of tariff volatility](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-leading-cpg-brands-are-using-ai-to-get-ahead-of-tariff-volatility) .


Brands that invest in big data and advanced analytics get more efficient, see further into their supply chain, and sell more.
